headline: The S&P fell 0.3% while Alphabet fell 12.6% — the index is now a hostage to five tickers, and the money that escaped went into defensives wearing a breadth costume.
summary: What changed overnight is that the bond market finally got paid for the crude rollover. The entire curve dropped 7bp today — 2y 4.61, 5y 4.78, 10y 4.98, 30y 5.32 — and is now 27-28bp lower on the month, with the 10y real yield down 28bp to 2.63 and MOVE -12.3% on the month at acceleration -2.23. The rates composite improved to -31 from -35. But look at the front: the 3-month bill is unchanged at 4.18%, +36bp over three months. Warsh's Fed held on Oct 28 and upgraded its description of activity; this is not a cutting cycle, it is term premium and inflation credibility being handed back. 3m10y flattened 21bp on the month to 0.80. The one thing that did not improve: the inflation composite is -51, still the worst number on the sheet, with WTI at 102.82 (+15.0% on the month, +79.1% YTD), DBC in the 97th percentile, oil/gold in the 98th, the 5-year breakeven +13bp on the month to 2.47 and turning up, and the 30-year mortgage at 7.24% — up 21bp on the month even as the 10y fell 28bp. Risk regime -12 vs -11.

The rupture was single-name and it was enormous. GOOGL -12.6% on Q3 results, a z=-2.28 move and the biggest one-day score anywhere on the board, dragging XLC -1.9% to the 0th percentile of its 52-week range and -9.2% on the month. MSFT, printing the opposite number, was flat at -0.2% and sits 21.4% above its 200-day. NDX -1.4%, QQQ/SPY acceleration -2.02, semis -7.5% on the month with SMH/SPY z=-1.49. Against that, the median stock ripped: equal-weight +1.2% at the 96th percentile, RSP/SPY +1.6% with acceleration 2.96 — the highest reading on the entire sheet — IWM +1.0% and +2.7% on the week, retail +2.6%, homebuilders +3.5%. Read the composition before you celebrate it. SPLV +1.7% at z=2.06/acc 2.46, USMV 97th percentile, XLP and XLU both accelerating above 2.0, MCD acc 2.94, HD acc 2.73, and high-beta/low-vol -11.4% on the month at z=-1.87. This is not animal spirits broadening out; it is duration-sensitive defensives absorbing capital evicted from the AI complex.

The cycle signal is worse than the index. CAT -9.2% today, -21.5% on the month, z=-2.58, 19.7% below its 200-day — the second-largest negative z on the board and the one stock whose order book is a macro series. XLI rolled over with relative strength -8.0% over three months, DJT is rolling over, XTN -9.1% over three months, growth pulse -2. But copper is +0.5% on the month, copper/gold is in the 98.5th percentile, and energy keeps leading: XLE +11.7% on the month with relative strength +10.9%, XOP +11.7%, XOM and CVX both in the 98th percentile. So this is a US capex and machinery problem, not a global demand collapse. On crude itself, yesterday's trade kept working: Brent -3.3% again to 111.48 while WTI was unchanged at 102.82, gasoline -5.4% on the month. The geopolitical premium keeps bleeding out of the waterborne barrel without touching the domestic one.

The periphery is where real damage is being done. Brazil lost 17.1% on the index and 20.8% in EWZ in a single week with USD/BRL +7.3%; USD/MXN is at the 100th percentile of the year, +5.0% on the month at z=1.82, even as Mexico's local index is +7.2%; EM/SPY is -7.6% on the month at z=-1.84; Turkey -11.5% on the month, Argentina at the 0th percentile. Korea's +6.6% index print is stale against EWY -2.5% and USD/KRW +0.9% — the won squeeze has now failed three separate times. Crypto gave back its bid again: BTC -3.3% to 78,621 and -28.6% over a year, ETH -4.0%, SOL -5.7% and -19.0% on the month, ETH/BTC in the 29th percentile, COIN in the 9th. Precious metals are still being liquidated rather than sold — platinum -4.0% at the 0th percentile, silver -14.2% on the month, GDXJ -12.8%, gold/silver z=1.87. And credit quietly refused to confirm the equity bounce: HYG/IEF -0.5% today and -1.6% on the month at z=-1.27, SKEW +4.5% on the month. Vol at VIX 17.2, the 21st percentile, is the cheapest thing you can own into this.

good.text: The whole curve re-priced lower: 2y 4.61, 10y 4.98, 30y 5.32, all -27 to -28bp on the month, with the 10y real yield at 2.63 (-28bp) and MOVE -12.3%. TLT +4.6% on the month. That is genuine multiple support for anything with a long duration cash flow.

Breadth is accelerating hard: RSP/SPY +1.6% with acceleration z=2.96, the highest on the board, +4.3% on the month; equal-weight at the 96th percentile; IWM +2.7% on the week and midcaps turning up. The average stock is no longer being starved by the index.

Health care is the cleanest trend on the sheet: XLV +2.4% to the 100th percentile, +7.8% on the month at z=1.80 with relative strength +7.1%/+8.7% and rising, LLY +6.6% (+16.0% on the month, 100th percentile), IBB at the 100th, UNH +9.6% on the month, medical devices accelerating at 1.78.

Financials are the only cyclical group whose relative strength is turning up: XLF +1.4% and +5.4% on the month at z=0.81, KRE +4.3% on the month, JPM +1.3% with acceleration 0.96, insurance accelerating at 1.94. Banks like the flatter, lower curve.

Credit refuses to crack at the index level: leveraged loans at the 100th percentile of the year, HYG flat on the day and +0.7% on the month, LQD +2.2% on the month, VIX 17.2 at only the 21st percentile. No funding stress is leaking from the equity rotation.

The dollar eased without a growth scare: DXY -0.3%, EUR +0.6%, GBP +0.6%, USD/CAD -0.5%, while copper held +0.5% on the month and copper/gold sits in the 98.5th percentile. Industrial demand is intact even as US machinery names break.

bad.text: Alphabet -12.6% on earnings, a z=-2.28 single-day move and the largest on the board, is -16.7% on the month and has pulled communications to the 0th percentile of its 52-week range (-9.2% on the month). META -15.5% on the month at acceleration -2.72, NFLX at the 0.1st percentile. Mega-cap concentration risk is now realizing, not theoretical.

CAT -9.2% today, -21.5% on the month, z=-2.58, 19.7% below its 200-day. Industrials rolled over with relative strength -8.0% over three months, transports rolling over, equal-weight trucking -9.1% over three months. The cycle bellwether is in a drawdown the index is not reflecting.

The inflation composite deteriorated again to -51, the worst number on the sheet. WTI 102.82 (+79.1% YTD), DBC in the 97th percentile, oil/gold in the 98th, the 5-year breakeven +13bp on the month to 2.47 and turning up, and the 30-year mortgage at 7.24% — 21bp higher on the month while the 10y fell 28bp. Mortgage spreads are widening into the bond rally.

Risk appetite is leaking where it always leaks first. BTC -3.3% to 78,621 (-28.6% y/y), ETH -4.0% and -15.4% on the month, SOL -5.7% and -19.0%, ETH/BTC in the 29th percentile, COIN in the 9th. Every attempt to turn this up has failed within a week.

Latin America is unravelling fast: Brazil -17.1% on the week with EWZ -20.8% and USD/BRL +7.3%, USD/MXN at the 100th percentile (+5.0% on the month, z=1.82), EM/SPY -7.6% on the month at z=-1.84, Turkey -11.5%, Argentina at the 0th percentile. Rising dollar-funding stress in the periphery is not priced in US credit.

The quality of the rally is defensive and the fast accelerations prove it: SPLV z=2.06/acc 2.46, USMV at the 97th percentile, XLP acc 2.04, XLU acc 2.05, MCD acc 2.94, HD acc 2.73, with high-beta/low-vol -11.4% on the month at z=-1.87 and semis/S&P at z=-1.49. Credit also declined to confirm — HYG/IEF -1.6% on the month at z=-1.27 while SKEW climbed to 151.

trades.name: Equal-weight over Nasdaq
trades.line: LONG RSP / SHORT QQQ - breadth acc 2.96 vs mega-cap crack
trades.expr: Long RSP, short QQQ, dollar-neutral. Size 1:1 notional; alternatively buy RSP calls funded by QQQ calls (same expiry, ~2m).
trades.thesis: The index's return is hostage to a handful of names whose earnings are now repricing violently, while the median stock is being bid on a 28bp monthly drop in real yields. Alphabet's -12.6% is the proof of concentration risk; RSP/SPY's acceleration of 2.96 is the proof of where the money is going.
trades.trigger: RSP/SPY +1.6% today with the highest acceleration z on the whole board (2.96) and +4.3% on the month at z=2.23, versus QQQ/SPY -1.0% at acceleration -2.02 and -3.7% on the month; GOOGL z=-2.28, XLC at the 0th percentile.
trades.stop: QQQ/SPY reclaiming its 200-day (ext back above 0%) or RSP/SPY giving back the entire month (<0.274). A semis re-acceleration — SMH/SPY back above z=0 — also kills it.
trades.target: RSP/SPY +5% from here (toward 0.300), roughly 500-700bp of pair P&L.

trades.name: Health care leadership
trades.line: LONG XLV - 100th pctile, LLY +6.6%, rel strength turning up
trades.expr: Buy XLV outright; express the beta with LLY and UNH as the single-name sleeve, or Jan XLV call spreads.
trades.thesis: This is the only group with a 100th-percentile price, a positive z-score on the month, and relative strength rising over both 1m and 3m. It is defensive enough to survive the mega-cap de-rating and cheap enough on relative multiples to keep absorbing rotation flows.
trades.trigger: XLV +2.4% today, +7.8% on the month at z=1.80, relative strength +7.1% (1m) and +8.7% (3m) and turning up; LLY +6.6% to a 52-week high (+16.0% on the month), IBB at the 100th percentile, medical devices accelerating 1.78.
trades.stop: XLV relative strength vs S&P rolling over (1m rs < 0) or a close back below the 200-day; LLY losing 1,200.

trades.name: Crypto beta
trades.line: SHORT MSTR - BTC 78.6k, SOL -19% m/m, every bounce fails
trades.expr: Short MSTR outright, or buy 2-3 month IBIT puts ~10% OTM to cap the squeeze risk. Pair against long SPY if you want the beta out.
trades.thesis: Crypto is the highest-beta read on risk appetite and it keeps failing to hold gains while the S&P sits near its highs. The equity wrappers carry the leverage and the balance-sheet premium decays faster than spot when spot stops going up.
trades.trigger: BTC -3.3% to 78,621 and -28.6% over the year; ETH -4.0% and -15.4% on the month; SOL -5.7% and -19.0%; ETH/BTC at the 29th percentile; COIN at the 9th percentile and rolling over; MSTR -8.4% on the month with acceleration -0.64.
trades.stop: BTC back above 86,000 (reclaiming the month's loss) or MSTR closing above 160.

trades.name: Energy over industrials
trades.line: LONG XLE / SHORT XLI - oil leads, CAT -21.5% on the month
trades.expr: Long XLE (or XOM/CVX 50-50), short XLI. Equal notional.
trades.thesis: The inflation composite is -51 and oil is up 79% YTD, so the cash flow is accruing to the producers; meanwhile the machinery/capex complex is in an outright drawdown that the index has not discounted. This is the cleanest way to be long the inflation that is actually happening and short the growth that isn't.
trades.trigger: XLE +11.7% on the month at z=1.18 with relative strength +10.9%/+12.7% and rising, XOM and CVX in the 98th percentile; XLI rolling over with 3m relative strength -8.0% and CAT -9.2% today, -21.5% on the month at z=-2.58.
trades.stop: WTI below 92 (giving back the month's +15%), or XLE relative strength 1m turning negative.

trades.name: 5-year breakevens
trades.line: LONG 5y breakeven vs nominal - BE +13bp while 5y fell 28bp
trades.expr: Buy 5y TIPS against short 5y nominal Treasuries (DV01-neutral); retail proxy is long TIP vs short IEF.
trades.thesis: The nominal curve has rallied 28bp on the month on the Fed's hold and a credible-inflation narrative, but the realized inflation inputs went the other way: crude +15% on the month, DBC in the 97th percentile, mortgages up 21bp. The front breakeven is the only series telling the truth and it is still only 2.47.
trades.trigger: 5y breakeven +13bp on the month to 2.47 and turning up while the 5y nominal fell 28bp to 4.78 and the 10y breakeven was flat at 2.35 — a 12bp 5s10s breakeven inversion into an oil-led CPI (headline CPI index z=0.65 and rising).
trades.stop: WTI below 92 and the 5y breakeven back under 2.33.

trades.name: Developed ex-US over EM
trades.line: LONG EFA / SHORT EEM - LatAm unravels, EM/SPY z=-1.84
trades.expr: Long EFA, short EEM, equal notional. Cheaper variant: long EWG/EWU basket vs short EWZ.
trades.thesis: EM's drawdown is concentrated in the currency: Brazil and Mexico are both bleeding through FX while their local indices hold up, which is how real EM dislocations start. Europe is doing the opposite — DAX, EWG and EWU all turning up with the euro firming.
trades.trigger: EM/SPY -7.6% on the month at z=-1.84 and rolling over vs EFA/SPY flat with positive acceleration; EWZ -20.8% on the week with USD/BRL +7.3%; USD/MXN at the 100th percentile; Hang Seng at the 8th percentile. EFA +0.6% today, EWG +1.5%, EWU +0.9%, EUR +0.6%.
trades.stop: USD/BRL back below 5.10 and USD/MXN below 18.00, or EEM/SPY reclaiming its 200-day.

trades.name: Housing on a false rate signal
trades.line: SHORT ITB - mortgage 7.24% while 10y fell 28bp; fade the pop
trades.expr: Short ITB or XHB after today's +3.5%, or buy Jan ITB puts ~7% OTM. Half size.
trades.thesis: Builders rallied on a Treasury move they are not receiving. The primary-secondary mortgage spread is widening, not compressing — the 30-year mortgage rose 21bp on the month against a 28bp drop in the 10-year. Until the mortgage rate actually falls, this is a rate-beta trade with no rate.
trades.trigger: ITB +3.5% and XHB +3.4% today, with XHB/SPY accelerating at 1.22, yet both still in a down trend, 3% below their 200-days and in the 30th percentile of the year; MORTGAGE30US 7.24% at the 89th percentile and in an uptrend.
trades.stop: 30-year mortgage below 6.95%, or ITB closing above its 200-day (≈95.4).
